subject: Recap & next steps: ACME POC scope & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps: ACME POC scope & success criteria

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. This thread is a quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan for the POC. Please reply with any edits and we can lock the timeline.

High-level POC goals (as discussed):
1) Support triage & summarization — classify inbound tickets and produce 1-2 sentence summaries that help agents.
2) KB retrieval + reranking — surface top answers from your internal KB and rerank by relevance/precision.
3) Semantic search / embeddings — improve search recall for product docs.

Success criteria (initial):
- Relevance: top-1 answer accuracy >= 70% on the evaluation set you provide.
- Latency: p95 inference < 500ms for single-turn queries on the dedicated test profile.
- Summarization quality: average human rating >= 4/5 on 50 sampled tickets.
- Cost target: <= $25 per 1k user-facing tokens (we'll monitor during trial).

Proposed timeline (flexible):
- Kick-off: week of Jun 22 (data ingestion/permissions)
- Baseline data ingest & schema mapping: by Jun 26
- Initial infra + model selection, first runs: by Jul 3
- Evaluation window: Jul 3-17 (2 weeks)
- Final review & decision: week of Jul 20 (decision by Jul 24)

Owners:
- ACME: Elena (product), Tom (eng) — data & eval access
- Redwood: Marissa (AE, program lead), Priyom (SE, technical lead), Neha (CS/ops)

Immediate next steps:
- I attached the POC requirements template (Attachment: acme_poc_requirements.xlsx). Please fill the data access section and share sample records (anonymized) by Jun 26.
- Priyom will reach out to schedule a 60-min tech kick-off the week of Jun 22.
- I'll share HubSpot and the SOW link after you confirm the timeline.

Thanks — excited to run this with you.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(Attachment: acme_poc_requirements.xlsx)

Thanks Marissa — this looks correct and aligns with what we discussed. Two quick items from our side:

1) We want to add a stretch use case to the POC: legal/contract summarization & clause detection for inbound legal intake. Would you be able to include a lightweight evaluation for that? We can provide ~200 sample contracts (anonymized) by Jun 30. The primary success criterion there would be correct identification of key clauses (NDA, termination, arbitration) with acceptable precision.

2) If we add that, will it materially change the timeline or cost? We want to avoid pushing the decision out too far — ideally still complete by late July.

If adding the contract use case requires extra annotation, we can coordinate with our legal ops team (copied) but please let us know what you need.

Thanks,

Elena — thanks for the note and for offering the contract samples. We can include contract summarization as a stretch use case. A few points and a suggested re-baseline so expectations are clear: 

Impact of adding contract use case:
- Scope: treat it as a stretch goal to be validated during the evaluation window. We'll run a separate contract extraction evaluation on the 200 samples you provide.
- Additional metrics: clause detection F1 >= 0.60 (stretch target), precision on key clauses >= 0.65.
- Annotation: to get reliable metrics we'll likely need 200-300 labeled clause examples; if ACME can provide a small set of labeled samples that will speed validation.

Proposed re-baseline (to accommodate extra eval):
- Baseline ingest & KB mapping: by Jun 26 (unchanged)
- Contract sample delivery: Jun 30 (ACME)
- Initial model runs (support triage + KB): by Jul 3 (unchanged)
- Expanded evaluation window (includes contract eval): Jul 3-Jul 24 (3 weeks)
- Final review & decision: week of Jul 27 (decision by Jul 31)

Notes on timeline & cost:
- Engineering/SE work: small increase (estimated +8-12 SE hours for creating contract eval harness).
- Annotation budget: if ACME provides labeled examples we can use those; otherwise we recommend a lightweight annotation run (we can estimate cost once we see sample density).

If that works, I'll revise the POC requirements doc and send a v2 with the contract section filled out and the updated timeline + owners. Please confirm and I will: (1) update the HubSpot deal with the new timeline, (2) send an updated SOW link for signatures if needed, and (3) Priyom will start prepping the evaluation harness.

Thanks — looping Priyom & Vivek for visibility.

—
Marissa Cole
